author: pgaudet
body:
Following up on https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/32284

Claude commented : 

## The HLA-DQA1 annotation is wrong

> This is the real error, and it is on the annotation side rather than in the ontology. Ten annotations to GO:0032395 are on MHC class II chain genes — the ligand, not the receptor — which is exactly what the term comment prohibits:

> | Gene | Evidence | Reference | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| HLA-DOA | TAS | PMID:3000765 | UniProt |
| HLA-DOB | TAS | PMID:2998758 | UniProt |
| HLA-DPA1 | NAS | PMID:2461352 | UniProt |
| HLA-DQA1 | NAS | PMID:3584986 | UniProt |
| HLA-DQA1 | NAS | PMID:6415485 | UniProt |
| HLA-DQA1 | TAS | PMID:2300572 | UniProt |
| HLA-DQA2 | NAS | PMID:3036828 | UniProt |
| HLA-DQB1 | NAS | PMID:2998758 | UniProt |
| HLA-DQB2 | NAS | PMID:2564844 | UniProt |
| HLA-DRB3 | NAS | PMID:6414998 | UniProt |

> All NAS/TAS, all from UniProt, none with `contributes_to`. They should be removed. HLA-DQA1 already carries the annotations it needs — `GO:0042605 peptide antigen binding`, plus the MHC class II protein complex on the component side — so nothing is lost by dropping them.

> The same error class affects the class I term, GO:0032393: six ComplexPortal annotations of the MHC class I–B2M complexes themselves (`hlaa-b2m_human` through `hlag-b2m_human`, all NAS), plus MR1 (TAS), which is an MHC class Ib molecule rather than a receptor for MHC class I. Correcting these is for the annotation providers, not the ontology.

> That answers your question about what the term represents: annotations to it are supposed to be TCR/CD3 components, and the HLA class II entries sitting alongside them are the reason the term looked like it meant two different things at once.
title: Review annotations to GO:0032395 MHC class II receptor activity

author: Antonialock
body: I removed these, apologies for the delay.
